title: Learning the Covariance of Treatment Effects Across Many Weak Experiments

problem.claim: When primary objectives are insensitive or delayed, experimenters need proxy metrics derived from secondary outcomes to estimate longer-term intervention impacts.

gap.claim: Even with many experiments, weak treatment effects can make the covariance of estimated treatment effects across experiments highly biased.

contributions.claim: The paper applies techniques inspired by weak instrumental variable analysis to address bias in covariance estimation under weak treatment effects.
It relates LIML and JIVE to alternative covariance-related estimands and presents a total covariance estimator under homoskedasticity.
It describes using the learned parameters to construct unbiased proxy metrics under various structural models and discusses an application at Netflix.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LIML learns a parameter equivalent to fitting total least squares to a transformed treatment-effect scatterplot.
The authors report that JIVE learns another parameter computable from the average of Jackknifed covariance matrices across experiments.
The authors report a Netflix application of their methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Delayed or insensitive primary objectives motivate proxy metrics based on secondary outcomes.
The paper studies meta-analysis across historical experiments to learn treatment-effect covariance, while noting severe bias when effects are weak.
Weak-instrument-inspired techniques are used, with LIML, JIVE, and a homoskedastic total covariance estimator characterized through related estimators.
The learned parameters are used to construct unbiased proxy metrics under structural models and are discussed in a Netflix application.

source_observation.claim: The methods target proxy metrics when primary outcomes are delayed or insensitive.

interpretation.claim: Covariance information across treatment effects can support proxy construction for longer-term outcomes.

application.claim: Organizations with many historical experiments may use cross-experiment treatment-effect covariance to design proxy metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide the structural-model assumptions required for unbiasedness.

unknowns: The abstract does not report quantitative results or comparisons.
The structural models and assumptions underlying unbiased proxy construction are unspecified.
The Netflix application details and outcomes are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
